s: Who launched Nano DAP in April 2023?
x: Amit Shah launched IFFCO's Nano DAP (8% N, 16% P) in April 2023.

s: Who sets the MRPs of P&K fertilisers under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme (2010)?
x: Under NBS, covering 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers, manufacturers set the MRPs themselves.

s: Under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme, the yearly fixed subsidy per kilogram is announced for which nutrients?
x: NBS provides a fixed per-kilogram subsidy on nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur, announced annually.

s: What does neem coating of urea mainly do?
o: Slows nitrogen release and stops diversion of farm urea to industry
Raises the potassium content of urea
Increases diversion of urea to industry
x: Neem coating slows nitrogen release and stops diversion of subsidised farm urea to industry.

s: Under PM-PRANAM, approved on 28 June 2023, States receive what share of the fertiliser subsidy saved by reducing chemical fertiliser use?
x: PM-PRANAM allows States to retain 50% of the subsidy saved through reduced chemical fertiliser consumption.

s: When did Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in fertiliser subsidy begin on a pilot basis?
x: Fertiliser DBT began as a pilot in October 2016 (PYQ key), with subsidy paid to companies after sale at PoS devices. September 2015 is when neem coating became mandatory for domestic urea; 2010 is when NBS was introduced; June 2023 is when PM-PRANAM was approved.

s: Why is the urea-centred fertiliser subsidy regime mainly criticised?
x: A urea-centred subsidy distorts the balance among nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (the NPK ratio).

s: What is the rank of the fertiliser subsidy among India's subsidies?
x: The fertiliser subsidy is the second-largest subsidy after the food subsidy.

s: What is India's rank among the consumers of fertilisers in the world?
x: India is the second-largest consumer and third-largest producer of fertilisers.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents India’s N:P:K fertiliser consumption ratio in 2023–24 and the ideal ratio respectively?
x: The 2023–24 N:P:K ratio was 10.9:4.1:1, against the ideal ratio of 4:2:1. The imbalance is associated with cheap urea and excessive nitrogen use.

s: One 500 ml bottle of IFFCO Nano Urea is claimed to replace which of the following?
o: one 25 kg bag of conventional urea
one 10 kg bag of conventional urea
one 50 kg bag of conventional urea
one 45 kg bag of conventional urea
x: A 500 ml bottle of IFFCO Nano Urea is stated to replace one 45 kg bag of conventional urea.

s: Which organisation developed Nano Urea and Nano DAP, applied mainly as foliar sprays?
x: IFFCO makes Nano Urea and Nano DAP; their claimed absorption efficiency is about 80%.

s: To whom is the subsidy paid under DBT in fertilisers?
o: fertiliser companies after sale at PoS devices
x: DBT pays the subsidy to companies after the sale is recorded on PoS devices, not to farmers.

s: How many grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers are covered under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme?
x: NBS (2010) covers 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about urea in India?
o: It is the most subsidised fertiliser
It remains under statutory price control
It gets a fixed per-kg subsidy under NBS
x: NBS covers P&K (and S); urea stays under statutory price control.

s: From which date did neem coating become compulsory for imported urea?
x: Neem coating was notified in May 2015, made compulsory for domestic urea from 1 Sep 2015 and for imported urea from 1 Dec 2015.

s: What is the nutrient content of Nano DAP?
x: IFFCO's Nano DAP has 8% nitrogen and 16% phosphorus.

s: What is India's rank in world fertiliser production?
x: India is the second largest consumer and third largest producer of fertilisers.

s: In which year was the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme introduced?
x: NBS (2010) gives a fixed per-kg subsidy on N, P, K and S for decontrolled P&K fertilisers.

s: What is the fertiliser subsidy allocation in the Union Budget 2026-27?
x: Budget 2026-27 gives Rs 1.71 lakh crore (RE 2025-26: Rs 1.86 lakh crore); it may reach about Rs 2.41 lakh crore as urea prices rose.

s: How much new urea capacity does the National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 add?
x: The National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 adds 10 MT of urea capacity.

s: Which State is the largest consumer of chemical fertilisers in India by total quantity?
x: Uttar Pradesh uses the most fertiliser in total (about 51.7 lakh tonnes of N+P+K nutrients in 2021-22); Punjab is high per hectare.

s: In which year was the World Bank-aided National Agricultural Technology Project (NATP) launched?
x: NATP began in 1998 with World Bank aid; its successor NAIP ran from 2006 to 2014.

s: Where is the Indian Institute of Millets Research located?
x: IIMR, like IIRR and IIOR, is located at Hyderabad.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: ICRISAT is at Patancheru (Hyderabad); CRRI is at Cuttack, IARI at New Delhi (Pusa) and CTRI at Rajahmundry.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Indian Institute of Maize Research — Ludhiana
Indian Institute of Millets Research — Ludhiana
Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research — New Delhi
x: The Indian Institute of Maize Research is located at Ludhiana. It should not be confused with the Indian Institute of Millets Research, which is located at Hyderabad; both use the acronym IIMR.

s: Where is the Central Tobacco Research Institute (CTRI) located?
x: CTRI is at Rajahmundry in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Where is the National Rice Research Institute (formerly CRRI) located?
x: CRRI, now the National Rice Research Institute, is at Cuttack.

s: During which period was the World Bank-aided NAIP implemented?
x: NAIP ran from 2006 to 2014 with World Bank support; NATP began in 1998.

s: Where is ICRISAT located?
x: ICRISAT is at Patancheru near Hyderabad.

s: Where is the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) located?
x: IARI is at Pusa, New Delhi.

s: Where is the Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research (IIOR) located?
x: IIOR, like IIRR (rice) and IIMR (millets), is in Hyderabad.

s:
Arrange the following ICAR initiatives in chronological order:
1. Lab to Land
2. Krishi Vigyan Kendra
3. National Agricultural Innovation Project
4. National Agricultural Technology Project
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The order is KVK (1974), Lab to Land (1979), NATP (1998) and NAIP (2006).

s:
Consider the following statements about ICAR's high-yielding varieties:
1. ICAR released 562 new high-yielding field-crop varieties during 2019-21.
2. More HYVs have been notified since 2014 than during the whole of 1969-2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ICAR released 562 new HYVs in 2019-21. Statement 2 is wrong: 3,236 HYVs were notified since 2014 against 3,969 in 1969-2014.

s:
Assertion (A): The genome-edited rice DRR Dhan 100 Kamala was developed from Samba Mahsuri.
Reason (R): Pusa DST Rice 1 was developed from MTU1010.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Kamala comes from Samba Mahsuri and Pusa DST Rice 1 from MTU1010; both are true but unrelated as cause and effect.

s: What is the percentage of crop area sown with certified or quality seed called?
x: SRR is the share of area sown with certified/quality seed; VRR is the share under varieties released in the last three to five years.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001?
o: Farmers may sell farm-saved seed as branded seed
Farmers may save, use, exchange and sell farm-saved seed
x: Farmers may sell farm-saved seed only as unbranded seed, so the branded-seed statement is false.

s: Under the Seed Village concept, which seed are farmers given to produce certified seed locally?
x: In a Seed Village, farmers receive foundation seed and produce certified seed locally.

s: The Varietal Replacement Rate is the share of area under varieties released in how many recent years?
x: VRR measures area under varieties released in the last 3-5 years.

s: Which body approves genetically modified crops in India?
x: GEAC approves GM crops under the Rules of 1989 framed under the EPA 1986.

s: Under which Act are the Rules for GEAC framed?
x: GEAC works under the 1989 Rules of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, in MoEFCC.

s: In which year did GEAC clear GM mustard DMH-11?
x: GEAC cleared DMH-11 in 2022; it is under Supreme Court scrutiny.

s: Why do genome-edited SDN-1 rice varieties fall outside GMO rules?
x: SDN-1 edits carry no foreign DNA, so DRR Dhan 100 Kamala and Pusa DST Rice 1 are outside GMO rules.

s: How many crop varieties were released in January 2026?
x: In January 2026, 184 varieties of 25 crops were released, including 122 cereals and 24 cotton varieties.

s: From which rice variety was India's first genome-edited rice, Pusa DST Rice 1, developed?
x: Pusa DST Rice 1 comes from MTU 1010, a Maruteru variety.

s: DRR Dhan 100 Kamala, a genome-edited rice, was developed from which Andhra Pradesh rice variety?
x: DRR Dhan 100 Kamala was developed from BPT 5204 (Samba Mahsuri), a Bapatla variety; Pusa DST Rice 1 came from MTU 1010.

s: Where was the first Krishi Vigyan Kendra set up in 1974?
x: The first KVK was set up at Puducherry in 1974 on the Mohan Singh Mehta Committee's recommendation.

s: Which committee recommended setting up the first Krishi Vigyan Kendra?
x: The Mohan Singh Mehta Committee recommended KVKs; the first came up at Puducherry in 1974.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA):
1. It is a demand-driven district-level extension society dating from 2005.
2. It plans its activities through Soil Health Cards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: ATMA is a demand-driven district extension society (2005). Statement 2 is wrong: ATMA plans through Strategic Research and Extension Plans (SREP), not Soil Health Cards. Hence 1 only (A); B, C and D wrongly accept statement 2 or reject statement 1.

s: Kisan Call Centres answer farmers' queries in how many languages?
x: KCCs (launched 21 January 2004) work in 22 languages from 17 locations.

s: Where was the Agriculture Integrated Command and Control Centre inaugurated in March 2024?
x: The Agriculture Integrated Command and Control Centre was inaugurated in March 2024 at Krishi Bhawan in Delhi.

s: Who launched the Kisan Call Centres on 21 January 2004?
x: The Department of Agriculture launched Kisan Call Centres (1800-180-1551) in 2004.

s:
Consider the following statements about Krishi Vigyan Kendras:
1. They are 100% funded by ICAR.
2. They are supervised through 11 ATARIs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: KVKs are fully ICAR-funded and work under 11 ATARIs.

s: In which year was ATMA, the demand-driven district extension society, set up?
x: ATMA dates from 2005; it plans through SREP.

s: Through which of the following is the extension principle 'seeing is believing' put into practice?
x: 'Seeing is believing' is the principle behind demonstrations.

s: What is the toll-free number of the Kisan Call Centres?
x: Kisan Call Centres answer on 1800-180-1551 in 22 languages from 17 locations.

s: What does the Meghdoot mobile app provide to farmers?
x: Meghdoot gives farmers weather-based agro-advisories in local languages.

s: Where was the first Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) set up in 1974?
x: The first KVK was set up at Puducherry in 1974; Pantnagar is the first agricultural university (1960).

s: What does Integrated Pest Management primarily combine?
o: Biological, cultural and need-based chemical control
x: IPM combines biological control, cultural control and need-based chemical control in order to reduce pesticide use.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Seeds Act, 1966 – quality of notified seeds
PPV&FR Act, 2001 – ban on GURT (terminator) seeds
x: The Insecticides Act 1968 set up the Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee; it has nothing to do with Seed Villages.

s: Which pesticide was associated with the killing of mugger crocodiles in Kota?
x: Aldrin was linked to the killing of mugger crocodiles in Kota; Endosulfan was banned by the Supreme Court in 2011.

s: Which of the following bodies is set up under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, 1971?
x: The Act and Rules set up the Central Insecticides Board and the Registration Committee.

s: The Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 would replace the Insecticides Act of which year?
x: The draft Bill would replace the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971.

s: Who banned Endosulfan in India in 2011?
x: The Supreme Court banned endosulfan in 2011.

s: How are neem-based products used in plant protection classed?
x: Neem-based products are bio-pesticides.

s: India still uses at least how many pesticides banned elsewhere?
x: India still uses at least 66 pesticides banned in other countries.

s: Which of the following is an advantage of chemical pesticides?
o: They leave no residue in food
They act quickly with high efficacy
They do not harm friendly insects
Pests never become resistant to them
x: Chemical pesticides control pests fast and effectively; residues and resistance are their drawbacks, so IPM uses them only when needed.

s: What is the estimated level of farm mechanisation in India?
x: India’s farm mechanisation level is reported as 40-45 percent.

s: To whom does Namo Drone Didi provide agricultural drones?
x: Namo Drone Didi gives drones to women SHGs.

s: Under Namo Drone Didi, central assistance covers what share of drone cost, up to Rs 8 lakh?
x: The scheme gives 80% central assistance up to Rs 8 lakh.

s: What is the drone target of the Namo Drone Didi scheme (2023-24 to 2025-26)?
x: It targets 15,000 drones with an outlay of Rs 1,261 crore.

s: Under which scheme are custom hiring centres and farm machinery banks subsidised?
x: SMAM (2014-15 to 2025-26) subsidises machines, custom hiring centres, hi-tech hubs and farm machinery banks.

s: What is the outlay of the Namo Drone Didi scheme for 2023-24 to 2025-26?
x: Namo Drone Didi has an outlay of Rs 1,261 crore to give 15,000 drones to women SHGs.

s: How often are Soil Health Cards issued to farmers free of cost?
x: Soil Health Cards (launched 2015) are issued free every two years.

s: Where was the Soil Health Card Scheme launched on 19 February 2015?
x: The scheme was launched at Suratgarh in Rajasthan on 19 February 2015.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Soil Health Card Scheme:
1. It is part of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (Soil Health Management).
2. The card gives soil nutrient status and fertiliser advice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The scheme falls under NMSA's Soil Health Management, and the card reports nutrient status with fertiliser advice.

s: By how much are Soil Health Cards estimated to have cut fertiliser use?
x: Fertiliser use fell by 8-10% and yields rose by 5-6%.

s: For what purpose is Glyricidia mainly used in agriculture?
x: Glyricidia is a green leaf manure (PYQ key). Neem-based products are the bio-pesticides, Kamala is a genome-edited rice, and Nano Urea or Nano DAP are the nano fertilisers.

s: Into which scheme was the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) merged from 2022-23?
x: NMSA, one of the eight NAPCC missions, was merged into PM-RKVY from 2022-23.

s: Who developed Zero Budget Natural Farming?
o: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority
x: Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by Subhash Palekar. Rythu Sadhikara Samstha only runs AP's natural-farming programme (APCNF), and APEDA handles NPOP organic certification.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about organic certification in India?
o: NPOP runs under the Commerce Ministry through APEDA
Under PKVY, clusters can be certified only through NPOP
PGS-India is an alternative certification route to NPOP
x: PKVY clusters may be certified by PGS-India or NPOP, not only NPOP.

s: What is the size of each organic farming cluster under the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY, 2015)?
x: PKVY promotes cluster-based organic farming with 50 farmers and 50 acres per cluster, certified through PGS-India or NPOP. The other combinations are not the PKVY norm.

s:
Consider the following statements about organic inputs:
1. Vermicompost is made by earthworms turning organic waste into manure.
2. Bt cotton is a green manure crop.
3. Sunn hemp and dhaincha are green manure crops.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Vermicompost uses earthworms, and sunn hemp and dhaincha are green manures. Bt cotton is a GM crop, not a green manure.

s: Which body handles organic certification under NPOP (2001)?
x: NPOP is run by the Commerce Ministry through APEDA; PGS-India is a separate certification route.

s: When was the National Mission on Natural Farming launched as a stand-alone mission?
x: NMNF began as a stand-alone mission in November 2024.

s: 'Har Medh Par Ped' is the agroforestry component of which mission?
x: NMSA's components are Rainfed Area Development, Soil Health Management and Agroforestry ('Har Medh Par Ped').

s: With which NMSA component is the slogan 'Har Medh Par Ped' linked?
x: 'Har Medh Par Ped' (a tree on every field bund) is the Agroforestry component of NMSA.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a green manure crop mentioned in relation to agricultural inputs?
x: Sunn hemp, dhaincha and green gram are mentioned in connection with green manure seed. Bt cotton is a genetically modified crop and is not a green manure crop.

s: What was the actual consumption of fertilizer in Andhra Pradesh as a percentage of allotment in 2015-16?
x: In 2015-16 AP used 80.78 per cent of its fertilizer allotment; this fell to 38.1 per cent in 2016-17 (AE).

s: Which body runs Andhra Pradesh Community Managed Natural Farming (APCNF)?
x: APCNF is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha and uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham.

s: APCNF received which award for the year 2024?
x: APCNF won the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in 2024.

s: What is the main function of Rythu Seva Kendras (formerly Rythu Bharosa Kendras)?
o: Village-level one-stop centres for agricultural services
x: Rythu Seva Kendras are village one-stop centres providing agricultural inputs and services.

s: Under which scheme are permanent buildings for the rationalised Rythu Seva Kendras being taken up?
x: Permanent buildings for RSKs are coming up under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS).

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's fertiliser consumption in 2024-25?
x: AP consumed 39.39 lakh MT of fertiliser in 2024-25.

s: After rationalisation, how many Rythu Seva Kendras remain functional in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Rythu Seva Kendras were rationalised from 10,778 to 8,489.

s: APCNF uses which bio-inputs?
x: APCNF relies on jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham.

s: Pesticide use in Andhra Pradesh fell from 2,650 MT in 2014-15 to about how much in 2024-25?
x: AP's pesticide use fell from 2,650 MT (2014-15) to 1,716 MT (2024-25).

s: About how many farmers practised AP Community Managed Natural Farming (APCNF) in 2025-26?
x: APCNF covered 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha in 2025-26.

s: Which of the following is classified as an input subsidy rather than public investment in agriculture?
o: Construction of a major irrigation project
Establishment of an agricultural research institute
x: Fertiliser subsidy is an input subsidy and represents a current transfer. Irrigation projects, agricultural research and rural infrastructure are forms of public investment and capital formation.

s: How is Minimum Support Price (MSP) classified?
x: MSP is a price support measure; fertiliser, power, water, seed and credit support are input subsidies.

s: Which of the following is public investment (capital formation) in agriculture rather than an input subsidy?
x: PACS computerisation builds capital; power, fertiliser and credit subsidies are current transfers.

s: Which of the following describes PMKSY correctly?
o: Umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2015–16
x: The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana is an umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2015–16.

s: In which year was PM-KUSUM, which supports solar pumps and solarisation of farm pumps, launched?
x: PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its PMKSY role?
o: HKKP — minor irrigation, CAD&WM, RRR of water bodies and groundwater
AIBP — major and medium projects, including National Projects
Watershed Development — Department of Land Resources
PDMC — presently a component of PMKSY under Agriculture
x: PDMC was part of PMKSY during 2015–2021 but is now under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY), not presently under PMKSY.

s: With which of the following is Per Drop More Crop under PMKSY primarily associated?
x: Per Drop More Crop focuses on micro-irrigation. It was under PMKSY from 2015 to December 2021 and is now under RKVY.

s: Under which scheme has Per Drop More Crop been implemented after December 2021?
x: Per Drop More Crop ran under PMKSY from 2015 to Dec 2021 and is now under RKVY.

s: Command Area Development and Water Management falls under which PMKSY component?
x: Har Khet Ko Pani covers CAD&WM, surface minor irrigation, repair of water bodies and groundwater.

s: Up to what share of cost is the micro-irrigation subsidy under Per Drop More Crop?
x: Micro-irrigation subsidy is up to 55% of cost, for up to 5 ha per farmer.

s: Punjab is called the 'Granary of India' because it was the pioneer State of which revolution?
x: Punjab was the pioneer State of the Green Revolution and is hence called the 'Granary of India'.

s: Which of the following is the scientific core of the Green Revolution package?
x: Although the package included HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, assured irrigation, pesticides and mechanisation, the scientific core was the use of HYV seeds.

s: In which crop did the Green Revolution first bring the biggest rise in output?
x: Mexican dwarf wheats raised wheat output from 5 to 17 MT; the gains were largest in wheat.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Green Revolution:
1. It was most successful in irrigated regions such as Punjab.
2. Its benefits were spread evenly over the rainfed regions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The seed-fertiliser-water package worked where irrigation existed (Punjab); its benefits went mostly to prosperous regions.

s: Which was the first crop transformed by the Green Revolution, and which was its pioneer State?
x: Wheat was the first crop transformed by the Green Revolution and Punjab was the pioneer state. Rice gained in a wider, later phase, including in the AP and TN deltas; Haryana gained but was not the pioneer.

s: Besides HYV seeds, which of the following were part of the Green Revolution package approach?
o: Withdrawal of price support and formal credit
Rainfed farming with traditional seeds only
Assured irrigation, chemical fertilisers and institutional credit
x: The package combined HYV seeds with assured irrigation, fertilisers, pesticides, mechanisation, institutional credit and MSP or assured procurement.

s: Which feature of HYV crops helps them resist lodging?
x: The short stature of HYVs helps them resist lodging; quicker maturity is what permits double cropping.

s: What does the quicker maturity of HYV crops allow?
x: HYVs mature quicker, making double cropping possible.

s: Which of the following was NOT part of the focus of the proposed Second Green Revolution?
o: Exclusive expansion of chemical pesticide use
x: The Second Green Revolution focused on pulses, oilseeds, millets, precision farming and micro-irrigation, not on expanding chemical pesticide use.

s: Who made the call for a Second Green Revolution in India?
x: The call for a Second Green Revolution was made by PM Manmohan Singh (APPSC 2025). M.S. Swaminathan coined the related term 'Evergreen Revolution', and Norman Borlaug is linked with the original Mexican dwarf wheats.

s: What does the concept of the Evergreen Revolution, associated with M.S. Swaminathan, mean?
o: Replacement of all traditional crops by HYV crops
Permanent increase in productivity without ecological harm
Expansion of agriculture only through irrigation-intensive farming
Continuous use of chemical inputs irrespective of environmental effects
x: The Evergreen Revolution means productivity improvement in perpetuity without ecological harm.

s: BGREI aims to raise rice-based productivity in which region?
x: BGREI aims to raise rice-based productivity in eastern India through HYVs, irrigation, balanced nutrients and IPM.

s: In 2006, PM Manmohan Singh called for a Second Green Revolution at the 93rd Indian Science Congress held in which city?
x: The call came on 3 January 2006 at the 93rd Indian Science Congress in Hyderabad.

s: The theme of the M.S. Swaminathan Centenary Conference (August 2025) was 'Evergreen Revolution, The Pathway to ___'. Which word fills the blank?
x: The theme was 'Evergreen Revolution, The Pathway to Biohappiness'.

s: How many States are covered under BGREI?
x: BGREI covers 7 States: Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Eastern UP and West Bengal.

s: Which of the following is NOT a BGREI State?
x: Punjab is not covered; BGREI targets eastern rice States.

s: Which Prime Minister called for a Second Green Revolution at the 93rd Indian Science Congress in 2006?
x: PM Manmohan Singh called for a Second Green Revolution on 3 January 2006 at the 93rd Indian Science Congress, Hyderabad.

s: What does the 'Evergreen Revolution' concept of M.S. Swaminathan aim at?
o: Raising farm productivity in perpetuity without ecological harm
Doubling milk output through village cooperatives
Raising oilseed output through a technology mission
Expanding the area under wheat in north-western India
x: Swaminathan's Evergreen Revolution means raising productivity permanently without harming the ecology, through sustainable farming.

s: In which year was the Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI) programme launched?
x: BGREI was launched in 2010-11 to raise rice-based productivity in seven eastern States.

s: BGREI is a sub-scheme of which of the following?
o: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture
x: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India runs as a sub-scheme of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY).

s: Which mission is the current effort associated with the Yellow Revolution?
x: The current Yellow Revolution effort is represented by the National Mission on Edible Oils.

s: The Yellow Revolution, initiated during 1986–87, was associated with which of the following persons?
x: The Yellow Revolution of 1986–87, related to oilseeds and edible oils, is associated with Sam Pitroda.

s: With which mission did the Yellow Revolution begin in 1986?
o: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture
x: The Yellow Revolution began in 1986 with the Technology Mission on Oilseeds; it is now carried on by the National Mission on Edible Oils.

s: Which Union Agriculture Minister drove the policy shift towards the Green Revolution in India?
x: C. Subramaniam, as Union Agriculture Minister, drove the shift; Borlaug and Swaminathan had scientific roles and Kurien led the White Revolution.

s: In which year did Norman Borlaug receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
x: Borlaug won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

s: Who is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India?
x: M.S. Swaminathan is the Father of the Green Revolution in India; Borlaug is its father in the world.

s: In which year did C. Subramaniam, who led the Green Revolution policy push, receive the Bharat Ratna?
x: C. Subramaniam, Union Food and Agriculture Minister (1964-66), got the Bharat Ratna in 1998.

s: Who was the Union Minister for Food and Agriculture (1964-66) who led the policy push for the Green Revolution?
x: C. Subramaniam, Union Minister for Food and Agriculture in 1964-66, led the Green Revolution policy push and got the Bharat Ratna in 1998.

s: Who among the following is associated with the Green Revolution in India and who with the Green Revolution at the global level, respectively?
x: M.S. Swaminathan is associated with the Green Revolution in India, while Norman Borlaug is associated with it at the global level.

s: What was the main aim of Operation Flood, implemented by the National Dairy Development Board from 1970?
o: Build a national milk grid based on the Anand cooperative model
Promote cotton exports through a technology mission
Expand marine fishing along the eastern coast
Increase oil-palm cultivation in rainfed areas
x: Operation Flood was run by the NDDB from 1970 and built a national milk grid on the Anand or Amul cooperative model.

s: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by which organisation?
o: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
x: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB).

s: Which Ministry launched White Revolution 2.0 in September 2024?
x: The Ministry of Cooperation launched White Revolution 2.0, which plans 75,000 new dairy cooperative societies.

s:
Consider the following statements about Operation Flood:
1. Phase I (1970-80) was financed by the World Food Programme.
2. Phase II (1981-85) raised milk sheds from 18 to 136.
3. The addition of 30,000 new dairy cooperatives came in Phase I.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: WFP financed Phase I and milk sheds rose from 18 to 136 in Phase II. The 30,000 new cooperatives came in Phase III (1985-96), not Phase I.

s: The White Revolution started in which State?
x: It started in Gujarat on the Amul model at Anand.

s: Who is known as the Father of the White Revolution?
x: Dr Verghese Kurien, who worked with Tribhuvandas Patel at Anand.

s:
Consider the following statements about the White Revolution:
1. NDDB was set up in 1965 to copy the AMUL model.
2. Operation Flood was the world's largest dairy development programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NDDB (1965) copied the AMUL model, and its Operation Flood (1970) was the world's largest dairy development programme.

s: White Revolution 2.0 aims to set up how many new dairy cooperative societies?
x: White Revolution 2.0 (Sept 2024) targets 75,000 new societies.

s: What was India's milk production in 2023-24?
x: India produced 239.3 million tonnes of milk in 2023-24 and is the world's largest milk producer.

s: Along with Verghese Kurien, who among the following is linked with building the Amul cooperative at Anand?
x: Dr Verghese Kurien worked with Tribhuvandas Patel at Anand to build the Amul three-tier cooperative.

s: The HYV programme became full-fledged from 1966 following which combination of circumstances?
o: Introduction of the WTO and the launch of PMKSY
Two successive drought years, decline in foodgrain output and dependence on PL-480
A sharp rise in foodgrain output and complete food self-sufficiency
Abolition of irrigation projects and withdrawal of fertiliser subsidies
x: The programme became full-fledged from 1966 after the 1965-66 and 1966-67 droughts, foodgrain production fell to 72.3 and 74.2 MT, and India depended on PL-480 supplies.

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. End of the first Green Revolution period
2. Intensive Agriculture District Programme (IADP)
3. Establishment of the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation
x: IADP came first (1960-61), then the first Green Revolution period ended, and MSSRF was set up in 1988.

s: In 1966, how much Mexican wheat seed was imported and crossed with local varieties in Punjab?
x: India imported 18,000 t of Mexican wheat in 1966.

s: Which years did the Early Green Revolution phase cover?
x: Pre-Green Revolution was 1951-68, Early 1968-81 and Later 1987-92.

s: In which year was the Intensive Agriculture District Programme (IADP) started?
x: IADP began in 1960-61, before the HYV programme of 1966.

s: In which year was the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation (MSSRF) set up?
x: MSSRF was set up in 1988; the first KVK came in 1974.

s: In the Rabi season of which year were HYV seeds first introduced in India?
x: HYV seeds came in the Rabi of 1966-67, during the Plan Holiday.

s: During which Plan period did the Green Revolution begin?
x: It began in the three Annual Plans of 1966-69 that followed the Third Plan.

s: Which was India's first agricultural university, linked with the Green Revolution?
o: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar
Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University, Guntur
x: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar (1960) was India's first agricultural university and is linked with the Green Revolution.

s: Which was the Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP) district in Andhra Pradesh?
x: IADP began in 1960 as a pilot in seven districts of seven States; West Godavari was AP's district.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Intensive Agricultural Area Programme (IAAP) began in which district?
x: IAAP in Andhra Pradesh began in West Godavari.

s: The Intensive Agricultural District Programme (1960) was piloted in how many districts?
x: IADP began in 7 districts of 7 States; IAAP later covered 114 districts.

s:
Consider the following statements about pre-Green Revolution programmes:
1. IADP (1960) began in 7 districts.
2. IAAP (1964-65) was extended to 114 districts.
3. IAAP in Andhra Pradesh began in East Godavari.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: IADP covered 7 districts and IAAP 114. In AP, IAAP began in West Godavari, not East Godavari.

s: Food self-sufficiency from the Green Revolution ended India's reliance on which of the following?
x: India stopped relying on PL-480 food imports.

s: Who is associated with the Red Revolution (meat and tomato)?
x: Red Revolution – Vishal Tewari; Pink – Durgesh Patel; Golden – Nirpakh Tutej; Blue – Hiralal Chaudhuri and Arun Krishnan.

s: With which of the following is the Golden Revolution associated?
x: Golden Revolution is horticulture and honey; jute is the Golden Fibre Revolution, cotton the Silver Fibre and eggs/poultry the Silver Revolution.

s: What does the expression 'Rainbow Revolution' refer to?
o: A programme limited to horticulture and honey production
Only the simultaneous growth of foodgrain and dairy production
The sequence of phases of the Green Revolution
The umbrella of colour revolutions covering crops, livestock and fisheries
x: Rainbow Revolution is the umbrella term for the different colour revolutions and represents holistic agricultural growth across crops, livestock and fisheries.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Round Revolution is associated with potato, not oilseeds. Oilseeds are associated with the Yellow Revolution.

s: 'Egg maximisation' and 'fisheries development' are associated respectively with which revolutions?
x: Egg maximisation is the Silver Revolution (eggs and poultry) and fisheries development is the Blue Revolution (APPSC 2018 keys). Golden is horticulture and honey, Pink is meat processing, prawn and onion, Yellow is oilseeds and Grey is fertilisers.

s: With which of the following is the Pink Revolution associated?
x: Pink covers meat processing, prawn, onion and pharmaceuticals (Durgesh Patel).

s: To which of the following does the Round Revolution relate?
x: Round Revolution = potato, not oilseeds.

s: Who among the following are associated with the Blue Revolution?
x: Blue Revolution (fisheries) is linked with Hiralal Chaudhuri and Arun Krishnan.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Revolution)
A. Golden Fibre
B. Silver Fibre
C. Grey
D. Round
List-II (Product)
1. Cotton
2. Jute
3. Potato
4. Fertilisers
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Golden Fibre is jute, Silver Fibre is cotton, Grey is fertilisers and Round is potato.

s: Who among the following is associated with the Pink Revolution?
x: The Pink Revolution (meat processing, prawn, onion) is associated with Durgesh Patel.

s: Who among the following is associated with the Golden Revolution?
x: The Golden Revolution (1991-2003) in horticulture and honey is associated with Nirpakh Tutej.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Revolution)
A. Yellow
B. Pink
C. Golden
D. Red
List-II (Person)
1. Nirpakh Tutej
2. Vishal Tewari
3. Sam Pitroda
4. Durgesh Patel
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Yellow - Sam Pitroda; Pink - Durgesh Patel; Golden - Nirpakh Tutej; Red - Vishal Tewari.

s: The Sweet Revolution is related to the production of which of the following?
x: The Sweet Revolution is related to honey (beekeeping).

s: Which scheme now carries forward the Blue Revolution in India?
x: The Blue Revolution (fisheries and aquaculture) is now carried forward by the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).

s: Which of the following pairs related to Green Revolution gains is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Imports India stopped relying on – PL-480
Foodgrain output in the mid-1960s – about 70-75 MT
Crop that gained most in the initial phase – Rice
x: Wheat gained the most in the initial phase; rice gained in a wider, later phase.

s: In which States were the early gains of the Green Revolution concentrated?
x: Punjab, Haryana and western UP gained most; the eastern rice states lagged.

s: Farmers holding more than how many hectares benefited most from the Green Revolution?
x: Farmers with more than 10 hectares benefited the most; the disparities were both regional and interpersonal.

s: The Johl Committee proposed shifting what proportion of paddy area as part of crop-diversification efforts?
x: The Johl Committee proposed shifting 20 per cent of the paddy area to address the problems associated with water-intensive rice-wheat monoculture.

s:
Consider the following statements about the costs of the Green Revolution:
1. Groundwater extraction in Punjab and Haryana is estimated to be 35-57% more than recharge.
2. The predominant N:P:K fertiliser ratio was balanced at 1:1:1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Groundwater extraction in Punjab and Haryana exceeds recharge by 35-57%. The N:P:K ratio was skewed at 10.9:4.1:1, not balanced at 1:1:1.

s: Which of the following is NOT an ecological cost of the Green Revolution?
x: N:P:K use became skewed at 10.9:4.1:1, not balanced; salinity, biodiversity loss and groundwater depletion were real costs.

s: Which crops were neglected by the Green Revolution?
x: Its crop bias neglected pulses, oilseeds and millets or coarse cereals.

s:
Assertion (A): The Green Revolution widened regional and interpersonal disparities.
Reason (R): Its gains went mainly to large farmers holding more than 10 hectares and to irrigated States such as Punjab and Haryana.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Gains went to large farmers and irrigated north-western States, which is why disparities between regions and between farmers widened.

s: Where was IR-8 rice developed?
x: IR-8 rice originated from the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) in the Philippines.

s: Which HYV wheat varieties are associated with Norman Borlaug's Mexican dwarf wheats?
x: Kalyan Sona and Sonalika were associated with HYV wheat derived from Norman Borlaug’s Mexican dwarf wheats.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a high-yielding variety or wheat selection?
o: Taichung Native-1 — First semi-dwarf rice introduced in India
Kalyan Sona — Mexican dwarf wheat developed by Borlaug
Lerma Rojo 64-A — Dwarf rice from the Philippines
x: Taichung Native-1, or TN-1, was the first semi-dwarf rice introduced in India in 1965. IR-8 was dwarf rice from IRRI, while Kalyan Sona was an Indian dwarf wheat selection and Lerma Rojo 64-A was Mexican dwarf wheat.

s: Which was the first semi-dwarf rice variety introduced in India (1965)?
x: Taichung Native-1 came in 1965; IR-8 is the IRRI 'miracle rice' of 1966.

s: Which rice variety is called 'miracle rice'?
x: IR-8, a dwarf rice from IRRI, Philippines, was called 'miracle rice'.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: TN-1 was India's first semi-dwarf rice; the IRRI 'miracle rice' was IR-8.

s: MTU rice varieties are associated with which research station?
o: Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi
Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, West Godavari
x: MTU varieties come from the Regional Agricultural Research Station at Maruteru in West Godavari. BPT varieties are associated with Bapatla.

s: Where was the BPT series of rice varieties developed?
x: BPT = Bapatla; MTU = Maruteru.

s: Which rice variety is known as Samba Mahsuri?
x: BPT 5204 (Samba Mahsuri) is a Bapatla variety and parent of DRR Dhan 100 Kamala.

s: In which areas of the south did the rice gains of the Green Revolution mainly come?
x: Rice gains came in the Godavari-Krishna and TN deltas.

s: Which one of the following crop–leading state pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Gujarat is the leading state for cotton, followed by Telangana and Maharashtra. Rajasthan leads rapeseed-mustard, Gujarat leads groundnut, and Madhya Pradesh leads soybean.

s: Which State is called the 'Rice Bowl of central India'?
x: Chhattisgarh is described as the 'Rice Bowl of central India'.

s: Which one of the following crop–leading state pairs is correctly matched?
x: Madhya Pradesh leads in pulses, followed by Rajasthan and Maharashtra. Uttar Pradesh, not Maharashtra or Gujarat, leads in sugarcane; Punjab is not a leading pulse state.

s: Which State is the leading producer of soybean?
x: Madhya Pradesh leads in soybean, not Maharashtra.

s: Which State is the leading producer of cashew?
x: Maharashtra (~25%) leads, followed by Andhra Pradesh (~17%) and Odisha.

s: Which State was the leading rice producer in 2024-25?
x: The rice leader moved from West Bengal (2021-22) to Telangana (2023-24) to Uttar Pradesh (2024-25).

s: Which State is the leading producer of rapeseed-mustard?
x: Rajasthan leads in rapeseed-mustard.

s: Which is the correct descending order of the following States in milk production (2019-20)?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat
Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh
Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat
x: In 2019-20 milk output ranked UP first, then Rajasthan, MP and Gujarat; AP was fifth.

s: Which is the correct descending order of the following States in cashew production?
x: Maharashtra leads cashew output (about 25%), followed by Andhra Pradesh (about 17%) and Odisha.

s: Which State was the leading rice producer in India in 2023-24?
x: The top rice State moved from West Bengal (2021-22) to Telangana (2023-24, UP second) and then to Uttar Pradesh (2024-25).

s: The Pulses Conclave 2020, held in Maharashtra, is a biennial global conference on which crops?
x: The Pulses Conclave is the biennial global pulses conference; its 2020 edition was held in Maharashtra.

s: Which State is the largest producer of wheat in India?
x: Uttar Pradesh leads wheat production, followed by Punjab, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh.

s: Which State is the largest producer of cotton in India?
x: Gujarat is the largest cotton producer, followed by Telangana and Maharashtra.

s: Which State is the largest producer of sugarcane in India?
x: Uttar Pradesh is the leading sugarcane producer of India.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank among States in milk production in 2019-20?
x: In 2019-20 the order was UP, Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat and then Andhra Pradesh at fifth place.

s: What was India's total foodgrain production in 2025-26 as per the second advance estimates?
x: Total foodgrain production reached 376.56 million tonnes in 2025-26.

s: What was India's horticulture production in 2024-25, which exceeded foodgrains?
x: Horticulture output was 367.72 MT, above foodgrain output of 357.73 MT.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the trend in India's foodgrain production from 2019-20 to 2024-25?
o: It fluctuated without any definite direction.
x: Foodgrain production recorded a steady increase over the period from 2019-20 to 2024-25.

s: Which of the following correctly describes India's position in pulses?
x: India is both the largest producer and the largest consumer of pulses, with production of 25.68 million metric tonnes as the cited latest figure.

s: What was India's foodgrain production in 1950-51?
x: Foodgrains rose from 50.8 MT in 1950-51 to 211.9 MT in 2001-02.

s: What was India's foodgrain production in 2018-19?
x: 2018-19 output was about 283 MT (3rd AE).

s: What was India's oilseed yield in 2024-25?
x: Oilseed yield reached 1,398 kg/ha in 2024-25.

s: What is the NMEO target for oilseed production by 2030-31?
x: NMEO aims at nearly 70 MT of oilseeds by 2030-31.

s: Since which year has India's horticulture output exceeded its foodgrain output every year?
x: Horticulture output has been above foodgrain output every year since 2012-13; in 2024-25 it was 367.72 MT against 357.73 MT.

s: What was India's record wheat production in 2023-24 (final estimates)?
x: Final estimates put wheat output at 113.29 MT in 2023-24, up from 110.55 MT in 2022-23.

s: Which of the following pairs on India's global rank is correctly matched?
x: India ranks first in shrimp output and exports, but second in fish production and aquaculture.

s: What is India's rank in the world in wheat and sugarcane production?
x: India is 2nd in wheat, sugarcane, fruits, vegetables, eggs, cotton and silk.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's global rank:
1. As of January 2026, India is the largest producer of rice, ahead of China.
2. India is the largest producer of fruits and vegetables.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India is now 1st in rice (150.18 MT vs China 145.28 MT). China is the largest producer of fruits and vegetables; India is 2nd.

s: In which of the following does India NOT rank first in the world?
x: India is 1st in milk, pulses and spices but 2nd in wheat.

s: What is India's rank in the world in fish production?
x: India is officially 2nd in fish production (about 8% of world output), though it is 1st in shrimp output and exports.

s: India's rice yield is about 2,929 kg per hectare. What is China's rice yield, approximately?
x: India's rice yield was about 2,929 kg/ha, compared with approximately 7,100 kg/ha in China.

s: To what level does the Kapas Kanti mission aim to raise cotton yield?
x: The Kapas Kanti mission targets a cotton yield of 755 kg per hectare.

s: Which States have the highest pulse yields in India?
x: Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat have the highest pulse yields, helped by black or semi-arid soils and high seed replacement rates.

s: Which State has the highest rice yield in India?
x: Punjab has the highest rice and wheat yields, thanks to canal and tubewell irrigation.

s: Which of the following is NOT a State with below-national-average rice yield?
x: AP, Telangana and TN are above the national average; Odisha, UP and Bihar are below it.

s: What is India's average cotton yield?
x: India's cotton yield is about 440 kg/ha against a global ~770; Kapas Kanti targets 755.

s: Which State has the highest wheat yield in India?
x: Punjab has the highest wheat yield (about 50 quintals per hectare) because of canal and tubewell irrigation.

s: Which soil is considered best for cotton cultivation?
x: Black (Regur) soil, which covers most of the Deccan Plateau, is best for cotton.

s: Agricultural yields fall by about how much for every 1°C rise in temperature?
x: Yields fall by about 8% per 1°C rise; a 1°C rise can wipe out about four years of rice and wheat productivity gains.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of El Niño on pulses?
o: Acreage rises by 2–9% and output rises by 6–30%.
Acreage falls by 2–9% and output falls by 6–30%.
Acreage falls by 6–30% and output falls by 2–9%.
Acreage remains unchanged while output rises by 5–25%.
x: In El Niño years, pulse acreage declines by about 2–9%, while output declines by about 6–30%.

s: Custom Hiring Centres raise farm productivity through which of the following?
x: Custom Hiring Centres serve mechanisation; better seed comes via SRR/VRR and genome editing, balanced nutrition via the Soil Health Card.

s: Cereal yield is the quantity of cereals produced per hectare of which land?
x: Cereal yield is measured in kilograms per hectare of harvested land under cereals.

s: Which one of the following crops is identified as an exception to India's generally lower yields compared with global averages?
x: India's yields of cereals, maize, soybean and pulses trail global averages, whereas groundnut is identified as an exception because of semi-arid concentration and improved varieties.

s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a major cause of India's cereal-yield gap?
o: Rainfed farming covering about 50–51% of net sown area
Universal access to efficient cold-chain infrastructure
Small and marginal holdings forming about 86% of holdings
A skewed NPK ratio and low seed replacement rate
x: Universal access to efficient cold-chain infrastructure is not a stated cause; rather, cold-chain losses account for about 30%. The other three factors contribute to the yield gap.

s: What does total factor productivity in agriculture refer to?
o: output growth not explained by growth in inputs such as land, labour, capital and fertiliser
the total value of agricultural exports divided by farm employment
output growth explained only by expansion of cultivated land
the ratio of fertiliser use to cropped area
x: Total factor productivity is the part of output growth that cannot be explained by increased use of inputs such as land, labour, capital and fertiliser.

s: About 67% of rice area is irrigated. What is the share for pulses?
x: Rice is ~67% irrigated against ~26% for pulses.

s: What is the extent of post-harvest cold-chain losses in Indian agriculture?
x: Cold-chain losses are about 30%; lack of cold chains is a cause of the yield gap.

s: A major criticism of India's agricultural growth is that it has come more from which of the following?
o: Improvement in yield than expansion of area
Expansion of area than improvement in yield
x: The criticism is that growth has depended more on area expansion than on yield improvement.

s: Which of the following drives total factor productivity growth in agriculture?
x: TFP is output growth beyond input growth; research, irrigation, roads, extension and education drive it.

s:
Consider the following statements about agricultural growth in India:
1. It has come more from area expansion than from yield.
2. Crop growth (3.5%) now leads livestock and fisheries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Growth comes more from area than yield. Statement 2 is wrong: livestock and fisheries now lead while crop growth lags at 3.5%.

s: After the decline in cotton area and output, what did India become?
o: A net exporter of raw cotton
A net importer of raw cotton
x: India became a net importer of raw cotton following declining cotton area and output.

s: Which crop's output fell to 290.91 lakh bales in 2025-26 from about 350 lakh bales?
x: Cotton area fell by 18 lakh ha and output declined to 290.91 lakh bales in 2025-26 from about 350 lakh bales.

s: By about how much did soybean area in Madhya Pradesh fall between 2023 and 2024?
x: MP soybean area fell 10%; 37.5% is the fall in Punjab's cotton area.

s: Telangana's cultivated area was 1.31 crore acres in 2014. What did it reach by FY23?
x: It rose to 2.2 crore acres via Kaleshwaram and Mission Kakatiya.

s: Which crops does the National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm (NMOOP, 2014) cover?
x: NMOOP covers oilseeds and oil palm; INSIMP covers millets and BGREI rice-based systems of eastern States.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income was set up in 2016 and reported in 2018
The National Commission on Agriculture was set up in 1970
The NCA submitted its final report in 1976
The Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income was chaired by M.S. Swaminathan
x: The Doubling Farmers' Income Committee was chaired by Ashok Dalwai, not M.S. Swaminathan.

s: In which year was the National Food Security Mission (NFSM) launched?
x: NFSM began in 2007-08 with rice, wheat and pulses and was renamed NFSNM in FY25.

s: With which revolution is the Technology Mission on Oilseeds (1986) associated?
x: The Technology Mission on Oilseeds (1986), later adding pulses and maize, is associated with the Yellow Revolution led by Sam Pitroda.

s: Under the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, 100% MSP procurement is provided for which pulses?
x: The mission (2025-26 to 2030-31) provides 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor.

s: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (2025-26 to 2030-31) is to cover how many low-productivity districts?
x: The scheme covers 100 low-productivity districts during 2025-26 to 2030-31.

s: The ‘Tilhan Mission’, referred to in February 2020, relates primarily to which of the following?
x: 'Tilhan' means oilseeds, so the Tilhan Mission (Feb 2020, PYQ) relates to oilseed production, in the line of the Technology Mission on Oilseeds and NMEO. Pulses have a separate mission (Aatmanirbharta in Pulses) and millets come under INSIMP.

s: Which crops does INSIMP, under RKVY, target?
x: INSIMP (2011-12) is for millets.

s: What was the National Food Security Mission renamed in FY25?
x: NFSM became NFSNM in FY25.

s: Who chaired the Doubling Farmers' Income Committee?
x: Ashok Dalwai chaired it (set up 2016, report 2018), not Swaminathan.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission on Agriculture:
1. It gave its final report in 1976 in 15 parts, including rural employment.
2. It was chaired by Ashok Dalwai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NCA reported in 1976. It was chaired by N.R. Mirdha; Ashok Dalwai chaired the Doubling Farmers' Income Committee.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses:
1. It runs from 2025-26 to 2030-31 with an outlay of Rs 11,440 crore.
2. It aims at 350 lakh tonnes of pulses from 310 lakh hectares.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The pulses mission (2025-26 to 2030-31, Rs 11,440 crore) targets 350 lakh tonnes from 310 lakh hectares.

s: Which scheme addresses the eastern rice States left behind by the Green Revolution?
x: Eastern rice States lagged after the Green Revolution, hence BGREI.

s:
Consider the following statements about Green Revolution outcomes:
1. It benefited wheat first, then rice.
2. It narrowed regional disparity among States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Wheat gained first, then rice. It widened, not narrowed, regional disparity.

s: The Green Revolution mainly benefited which regions?
x: Punjab, Haryana and western UP benefited; eastern rice States still lag.

s: With the production of which crops is the 'Tilhan Mission' associated?
x: Tilhan Mission refers to oilseed production.

s: In which Plan was the lowest agricultural growth of only 0.73% recorded?
x: The Third Plan recorded 0.73% agricultural growth; the Eighth Plan recorded 4.68% against a 4.1% target.

s: The share of agriculture in national income was 56.5% in 1950-51. To about what level has it declined?
x: Agriculture's share in national income declined from 56.5% in 1950-51 to about 18% in the current reference period.

s: The collapse of agricultural performance during the Third Plan, largely due to droughts, helped start which of the following?
x: The drought-related collapse during the Third Plan helped set off the Green Revolution.

s: In which Plan was the highest agricultural growth recorded?
x: The Eighth Plan recorded 4.68%, the highest, against a 4.1% target.

s: What was the agricultural growth rate at 2011-12 prices in 2015-16?
x: Agricultural growth in 2015-16 was about 0.7% at 2011-12 prices.

s: What was the agriculture and allied sector growth in Q1 FY27?
x: Q1 FY27 growth was 3.6%; FY26 (provisional) was 3.0% and FY24 was 2.7%.

s: Which of the following pairs on agricultural growth during FY16-FY25 is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: World average agricultural growth – 4.4% a year
x: 4.4% was India's agriculture and allied average; the world average was 2.9%.

s: In which years was agriculture and allied growth negative?
x: 2002-03 and 2014-15 were negative; 2015-16 grew about 0.7%.

s: What was India's average agriculture and allied growth during FY16-FY25?
x: FY16-FY25 averaged 4.4%, the highest decadal growth, against a world average of 2.9%.

s: What is the provisional agriculture and allied growth for FY26?
x: FY26 is 3.0% (provisional); Q1 FY27 is 3.6%.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Agriculture and allied growth was negative in 2002-03 and 2014-15.
2. The National Agricultural Policy 2000 set a growth target of over 4% per annum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: growth was negative in 2002-03 and 2014-15, and NAP 2000 aimed at over 4% growth a year.

s: What is the paddy yield of Andhra Pradesh, among the best in India?
x: AP's paddy yield is about 6 t/ha, among the best, though its foodgrain output fluctuates with the monsoon.

s: What was the rabi paddy yield of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
x: AP's rabi paddy yield was 6,979 kg/ha, higher than the kharif yield of 5,612 kg/ha.

s: The foodgrain production of Andhra Pradesh was 157.59 lakh tonnes in which year?
x: Andhra Pradesh produced 157.59 lakh tonnes of foodgrains in 2017-18.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's agriculture and allied growth in 2023-24, its only year of contraction?
x: Agriculture and allied growth was −1.58%; the −9.82% figure is the separate fall in the crops sub-sector.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's foodgrain production in 2025-26 (2nd AE)?
x: AP's 2025-26 output is 190.29 lakh t, up 17.03%.

s: From which year did the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture become a sub-mission of Krishonnati?
x: NMSA became a Krishonnati sub-mission from 2018-19 and was brought under PM-RKVY from 2022-23.

s: With reference to the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Per Drop More Crop – NMSA component
x: RAD, Soil Health Management and Per Drop More Crop are NMSA components; the National Agricultural Market (e-NAM) is not an NMSA component.

s: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana announced for 2025-26 is proposed as a Central Sector scheme covering:
o: All agricultural districts for five years
100 low-performing agricultural districts for six years
x: The scheme is proposed as a Central Sector scheme for 100 low-performing agricultural districts for six years.

s: What is the main aim of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY)?
o: Give grants to raise State spending on agriculture through State-led plans
Give interest subvention on crop loans
x: RKVY gives grants to raise State spending on agriculture through State-led agricultural plans; it now runs under PM-RKVY.

s: The National Food Security Mission was renamed as which of the following in Financial Year 2024-25?
o: National Food Security and Nutrition Mission
x: NFSM was renamed the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) in FY 2024-25.

s:
Consider the following statements about the funding pattern of the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH):
1. The Centre-State sharing ratio is generally 60:40.
2. The ratio is 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States.
3. The general sharing ratio is 50:50.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: MIDH follows 60:40 generally and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States; so statement 3 (50:50) is wrong.

s: What is the outlay of the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oilseeds, announced on 3 October 2024?
x: NMEO-Oilseeds has an outlay of ₹10,103 crore and aims to raise oilseed output from 39 MT to 69.7 MT by 2030-31.

s: Up to what share can the micro-irrigation subsidy be under the Per Drop More Crop component of NMSA?
x: Per Drop More Crop gives a micro-irrigation subsidy of up to 55%.

s: What is the outlay of the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (August 2021)?
x: NMEO-Oil Palm (Aug 2021) has ₹11,040 crore; ₹10,103 crore is the outlay of NMEO-Oilseeds.

s: At what interval are Soil Health Cards issued free under NMSA?
x: Soil Health Cards are issued free every two years, not annually.

s: Under which of the following is the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture one of the missions?
x: NMSA (2014-15) is one of the 8 missions of the National Action Plan on Climate Change.

s: Which programme was launched by ICAR in 2011 to make Indian agriculture resilient to climate change?
o: National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture
x: NICRA (National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture) was launched by ICAR in 2011; NMSA came later in 2014-15.

s: In which year was the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm launched?
x: NMEO-Oil Palm was launched in August 2021 with an outlay of ₹11,040 crore; NMEO-Oilseeds followed in October 2024.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA):
1. It is one of the eight missions under the NAPCC.
2. It has been under PM-RKVY since 2022-23.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NMSA is one of the 8 NAPCC missions and has been placed under PM-RKVY since 2022-23.

s: In which year was the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) launched?
x: RKVY was launched in 2007-08 to give grants that raise State spending on agriculture.

s: The National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm (2021) focuses mainly on which regions?
o: The North-East and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
x: NMEO-Oil Palm (August 2021, Rs 11,040 crore) focuses on the North-East and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

s: Under PM-AASHA, which component involves procurement by NAFED and NCCF?
x: The Price Support Scheme (PSS) under PM-AASHA involves procurement through agencies such as NAFED and NCCF.

s: The e-NAM platform was launched in April 2016 by which organisation?
x: e-NAM was launched in April 2016 by the Small Farmers’ Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC).

s: From 2021-22, Operation Greens (Budget 2018-19) was widened to cover what?
x: Operation Greens was widened from the original TOP commodities to 22 perishables from 2021-22.

s: With reference to PM-AASHA, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: PDPS covers 40% of State oilseed output; the Market Intervention Scheme covers 25%.

s: What is the full form of SFAC, which launched e-NAM?
x: SFAC is the Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium, which launched e-NAM in April 2016.

s: What is the purpose of Krishi UDAN?
o: Air transport of perishable farm produce
x: Krishi UDAN supports moving perishable farm produce by air; online trading is e-NAM.

s: In which year was PM-AASHA launched to ensure remunerative prices to farmers?
x: PM-AASHA came in 2018 with PSS, PDPS, MIS and the Price Stabilisation Fund.

s: Operation Greens, announced in the Budget 2018-19, was first aimed at stabilising the prices of which crops?
x: Operation Greens began with TOP (tomato, onion, potato) on the lines of Operation Flood; it was widened to 22 perishables from 2021-22.

s: Who chaired the National Commission on Agriculture (1970)?
x: NCA, set up in 1970, was chaired by N.R. Mirdha.

s: The National Commission on Agriculture, which submitted its report in 1976, was chaired by whom?
x: The National Commission on Agriculture functioned during 1970–76 and submitted its report in 1976 under the chairmanship of Nathu Ram Mirdha.

s: Which term was coined by the National Commission on Agriculture (1976)?
x: The National Commission on Agriculture recommended HYVs, irrigation and credit reforms and is associated with coining 'social forestry'.

s: At what level did the National Commission on Farmers (M.S. Swaminathan) recommend fixing MSP?
x: The NCF recommended MSP at C2 + 50%; 1.5 times A2+FL is the Government's present MSP policy.

s: When was the National Commission on Farmers constituted?
x: The NCF under M.S. Swaminathan was constituted on 18 November 2004 and gave 5 reports in 2004-06.

s: At what level does the government's present MSP policy fix MSP?
x: The government pays 1.5 times A2+FL; C2 + 50% was the Swaminathan Commission's recommendation.

s: For how many mandated crops does the government announce MSP?
x: MSP is announced for 22 mandated crops, at 1.5 times A2+FL.

s: What annual agricultural growth did the National Agriculture Policy, 2000 envisage?
x: The policy targeted agricultural growth in excess of 4% per annum.

s: Which broad-based revolution covering all farm sub-sectors did the National Agriculture Policy, 2000 envisage?
x: NAP 2000 emphasised a Rainbow Revolution across farm sub-sectors, along with private participation, price protection and insurance.

s: Which one of the following colour-crop pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Silver Revolution is associated with eggs. Fertilisers are associated with the Grey Revolution.

s: Which of the following was a thrust of the National Agriculture Policy, 2000 for private participation?
x: NAP 2000 sought private participation through contract farming and land leasing, along with price protection and national agricultural insurance.

s: In the Rainbow Revolution, to what does the Silver Revolution relate?
x: Silver stands for eggs; Blue is fisheries, Yellow oilseeds and Grey fertilisers.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Agricultural Renewal Action Plan:
1. It was proposed by the National Commission on Farmers.
2. 2006-07 was to be observed as the Year of Agricultural Renewal.
3. It aimed at bridging the gap between actual and potential yields.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: the NCF proposed the plan, with 2006-07 as the Year of Agricultural Renewal, to bridge the yield gap.

s: Which of the following is NOT a package of the Agricultural Renewal Action Plan?
x: The packages were soil health, water harvesting and efficient water use, credit and insurance reform, technology dissemination and market reform.

s: Who chaired the National Commission on Farmers constituted in 2004?
x: The National Commission on Farmers (2004) was chaired by M.S. Swaminathan; Radhakrishna headed the Expert Group on Indebtedness.

s: India’s entry into the WTO in 1995 was associated with which combination in the agricultural sector?
o: Reduced import competition and increased subsidies as a share of farm income
Increased import competition and declining subsidies as a share of farm income
Abolition of all domestic agricultural support
Reduced international trade and unchanged farm incomes
x: WTO entry increased import competition, while subsidies declined as a share of farm income.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the WTO treatment of the Amber Box?
o: It consists only of decoupled income support.
It is not trade-distorting and is freely allowed without limits.
It carries reduction commitments, subject to de minimis limits of 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.
It consists of payments tied to limiting production and has no reduction commitment.
x: Amber Box support is subject to reduction commitments, with de minimis limits of 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.

s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, which of the following falls in the Amber Box?
x: Price support is Amber Box; decoupled income support, environmental programmes and farmer training are Green Box.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Green Box – Trade-distorting support subject to limits
Amber Box – Minimal or no trade distortion
Blue Box – Amber-type support with production-limiting conditions
Amber Box – Support with production-limiting conditions
x: The Blue Box is Amber-type support with production limits; the Green Box causes minimal distortion and the Amber Box is distorting support subject to limits.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Amber Box under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture:
1. Production-linked subsidies are examples of Amber Box support.
2. Amber Box support is trade- or production-distorting and is subject to limits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the Amber Box covers trade- or production-distorting support subject to limits, so production-linked subsidies fall in it.

s: Which one of the following was an effect of liberalisation after 1991 on Indian agriculture?
o: Replacement of agricultural subsidies by foreign aid
Increase in government investment in agriculture in every period
A ban on all private participation in agriculture
Decline in government investment in agriculture
x: The stated policy impact of post-1991 liberalisation was a decline in government investment in agriculture.

s: Which genetically modified crop was approved for commercial cultivation in India in 2002?
x: Bt cotton, approved in 2002, is the only genetically modified crop identified as approved for commercial cultivation in India.

s:
With reference to the 1990s farmers' debate on the Dunkel Draft:
1. Sharad Joshi backed globalisation.
2. Mahendra Singh Tikait (BKU) backed the Dunkel Draft.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: Sharad Joshi backed globalisation, whereas Tikait (BKU) and Nanjundaswamy (KRRS) opposed the Dunkel Draft.

s:
Consider the following statements about WTO subsidy boxes:
1. The de minimis limit is 5% for developed countries.
2. The de minimis limit is 10% for developing countries.
3. MSP-based price support falls in the Green Box.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: De minimis is 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries; MSP is Amber Box support, not Green Box.

s: Farmer training falls in which WTO subsidy box?
x: Farmer training is minimally distorting and is permitted under the Green Box.

s: Which organisation compiles the Agriculture Orientation Index (SDG 2.a.1)?
x: The Agriculture Orientation Index, agriculture's share of government spending divided by its share of GDP, is compiled by the FAO, not IFPRI.

s: How many action points for farmers were announced in the Union Budget 2020-21?
x: The Union Budget 2020-21 announced 16 action points for farmers towards doubling income by 2022.

s: Rainfed farming accounts for approximately what share of India’s net sown area and food production, respectively?
x: Rainfed farming covers about 50–60% of net sown area and contributes approximately 40% of food production.

s: What is the main role of the National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA), set up in 2006?
o: Provides knowledge inputs and coordinates rainfed-area upgradation through a watershed approach
x: NRAA is an expert body that provides knowledge inputs and coordinates upgrading of dryland and rainfed areas through a watershed approach.

s: Sustainable agriculture seeks to combine environmental health and economic profitability with which of the following?
x: The three pillars of sustainable agriculture are environmental health, economic profitability and social and economic equity.

s: Sustainable agriculture is best understood as the use of land in a manner that:
o: Excludes all modern inputs from farming
Maximises present output regardless of future soil quality
Maintains land quality while meeting present needs without compromising future generations
Uses land only for export-oriented crops
x: Sustainable agriculture maintains the quality of land while meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.

s: In which year was the National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA) set up?
x: The NRAA was set up in 2006 to coordinate the upgrading of rainfed areas through a watershed approach.

s: The Ashok Dalwai Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income used which base year?
x: The base year was 2015-16, with 2022 as the target year.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the identified sources of growth in farmers’ income?
o: Exclusive dependence on traditional low-value crops
x: The seven sources include crop productivity, livestock productivity, resource-use efficiency, cropping intensity, diversification to high-value crops, better price realisation and movement to non-farm jobs. Exclusive dependence on traditional low-value crops is not one of them.

s: Towards what does the Doubling Farmers' Income approach shift the focus from production?
o: Income enhancement through value addition, market reform and post-harvest infrastructure
x: The approach shifts from 'production' to 'income' via value addition, e-NAM and APMC reform, post-harvest infrastructure and allied integration.

s: The Ashok Dalwai Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income set which target year?
x: The Dalwai Committee (2016-18) took 2015-16 as base year and 2022 as target year, in 14 volumes.

s: How many sources of growth in farmers' income did the Doubling Farmers' Income strategy identify?
x: Seven sources were identified, including crop and livestock productivity, cropping intensity, better prices and non-farm jobs.

s: In how many volumes did the Ashok Dalwai Committee submit its report on Doubling Farmers' Income?
x: The Dalwai Committee (2016-18) gave its report in 14 volumes, with base year 2015-16 and target year 2022.

s: Which reform area is associated with the Ashok Dalwai Committee?
o: DBT for food and decentralised procurement under the PDS
Value addition and land leasing in the context of doubling farmers’ income
Inflation targeting and monetary policy independence
x: Ashok Dalwai’s reform area concerns doubling farmers’ income, including value addition and land leasing.

s: Andhra Pradesh leads India in the area under which crop, with about 2.49 lakh hectares or 48% of the national area in 2024-25?
x: AP leads India in oil palm: 2.49 lakh ha (48% of India's area; earlier 2.27 lakh ha) and 22.81 lakh MT of fresh fruit bunches in 2024-25 (SES 2025-26). AP is not recorded as holding that position for cashew, coconut or cocoa.

s: What was the allocation for agriculture in the Union Budget 2026-27?
x: The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated ₹1.3 lakh crore to agriculture, representing a 2.6 per cent increase.

s: Whom does Andhra Pradesh's Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan scheme cover?
x: It covers landholders and tenant farmers; tenants are outside the central PM-KISAN.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Budget 2026-27 was presented by which minister?
x: The AP Agriculture Budget 2026-27 (about ₹53,753 crore, the third separate one) was presented by Minister K. Atchannaidu.

s: What was the annual assistance per family under the earlier YSR Rythu Bharosa scheme of Andhra Pradesh?
x: YSR Rythu Bharosa gave ₹13,500 per family a year, including tenant and RoFR farmers; Annadata Sukhibhava now gives ₹20,000.

s: From which date was PM-KISAN, a Central Sector scheme, made effective?
x: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme effective from 1 December 2018, paying Rs 6,000 a year in three instalments.

s: In the Early Green Revolution phase (1968-81), in which crop were HYV seeds first introduced?
x: HYV seeds came first in wheat; the Later phase (1987-92) spread the Green Revolution to rice and other regions.

s: The spread of the Green Revolution to rice and other regions marks which phase?
x: The Later Green Revolution (1987-92) spread the new technology to rice and other regions; the early phase began with wheat.

s: PL-480 imports and the droughts of 1965-67 belong to which phase of Indian agriculture?
x: The Pre-Green Revolution phase (1951-68) saw land reforms, irrigation, PL-480 imports and the 1965-67 droughts.

s: What is the HYV-seed, fertiliser and irrigation strategy of the Early Green Revolution phase (1968-81) known as?
x: The Early Green Revolution phase (1968-81), with HYV seeds, fertiliser and irrigation, is called the New Agricultural Strategy.

s: For Kharif 2026, the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister issued which directive regarding crop insurance?
o: Only loanee farmers' paddy crop to be insured, with banks accountable
Only horticulture crops to be insured, with FPOs accountable
Every cultivated crop to be insured, with District Collectors accountable
Insurance to be made optional for all crops, with Mandal officers accountable
x: In July 2026 the CM ordered that every cultivated crop be insured for Kharif 2026, making District Collectors accountable for coverage.

s: PMFBY, introduced in 2016, replaced NAIS and which other scheme?
x: PMFBY replaced NAIS (1999) and MNAIS (2010); WBCIS was not replaced.

s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the principle associated with PMFBY?
o: One Nation, One Farmer, One Subsidy
One District, One Crop, One Insurance
One State, One Crop, One Premium
One Nation, One Crop, One Premium
x: The principle associated with PMFBY is ‘One Nation, One Crop, One Premium’.

s: From which year did PMFBY become voluntary for all farmers?
x: PMFBY became voluntary in 2020; it covers pre-sowing to post-harvest losses.

s: For what is YES-TECH used under PMFBY?
x: YES-TECH is remote-sensing yield estimation; WINDS is weather stations, DigiClaim digital claims and RWBCIS weather-index insurance.

s: What is the farmer's premium share under PMFBY?
o: 2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi, and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops
1.5% for Kharif, 2% for Rabi, and 5% for commercial crops
5% for Kharif, 2% for Rabi, and 1.5% for horticultural crops
2% for all crops in every season
x: The farmer premium under PMFBY is 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops.

s: What did crop insurance in Andhra Pradesh under PMFBY/RWBCIS become from Rabi 2024-25?
o: Compulsory, with the State paying the full premium
Voluntary, with the Centre paying the full premium
Voluntary, with farmers paying a small fixed share and the State and Centre sharing the rest equally
Compulsory, with FPOs paying the premium
x: From Rabi 2024-25 enrolment became voluntary; farmers pay a small fixed share and the State and Centre share the balance equally.

s: Under Dr YSR Free Crop Insurance in Andhra Pradesh (2019-24), who paid the crop insurance premium?
o: The State and the Centre equally
x: The State paid the entire premium, and CCRC holders were covered.

s: When is a payout made under the Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS)?
o: Crop yield falls below the threshold yield
Observed weather deviates from specified trigger levels
The market price falls below MSP
The farmer's landholding is below one hectare
x: RWBCIS is weather-index insurance: it pays when weather deviates from predetermined trigger levels.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PMFBY?
o: Farmers pay 2% premium for Kharif crops
Farmers pay 1.5% premium for Rabi crops
It became voluntary for all farmers from 2020
It replaced the Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme
x: PMFBY (2016) replaced NAIS and MNAIS, not WBCIS.

s: For what is WINDS used under PMFBY?
x: WINDS is the weather information system; YES-TECH is for yield estimation.

s:
Consider the following statements about crop insurance cover:
1. Crop loss due to natural calamities, pests and diseases is covered.
2. Low yield caused by poor quality of seed is covered.
